hypothesis: Fuse delimiter discovery, field validation, and numeric conversion into one allocation-free byte parser while retaining the incumbent borrowed-key standard HashMap and final ordering. Round-1 development measurements improve all 8192-record cases (mean case log ratios about -0.10 to -0.54), but the 512-record high-cardinality cases still regress (+0.08 to +0.17); removing repeated parser scans should lower per-record work without adding another cardinality heuristic. ASCII endpoint control checks are fused with the first-TAB scan, and non-ASCII endpoints still use char::is_control. Numeric grammar and conversion share a scan. Status values reject monotonically above 599; byte fields of at most 19 digits cannot overflow u64, and longer fields use checked arithmetic to preserve both u64::MAX and arbitrarily many leading zeroes.
notes: Fresh model-authored revision based only on the exported round-1-clean application and development evidence. No compile, correctness execution, profiling or benchmark was run by the proposal author. The timing pattern suggests remaining parsing and fixed map/sort overhead but does not establish a profile. This change deliberately targets parsing only; hash/sort setup cost on small inputs may remain. Risks: a scalar endpoint scan may be slower than the standard delimiter implementation on very long endpoints, non-ASCII endpoints need a second control scan, and unusual long numeric fields pay checked-arithmetic overhead. Exact LF/final-LF and single terminal-CR handling remain unchanged; signs, whitespace, Unicode digits, extra TABs and overflow remain invalid. Only ASCII TAB boundaries slice str. No unsafe code, custom hasher, global state, caching, dependency or driver changes.
